verificationGuide.summary: Each entry carries a canonical COSE_Sign1 envelope (RFC 9052) over an in-toto v1 Statement payload. The chain links via sha256 of each envelope; when VAULT_SIGNING_KEY is configured, each envelope is Ed25519-signed and verifiable offline against the published verification keys. Verify the chain independently of this server before relying on it.
steps: Read `integrityLevel` and `signatureCoverage`. `hash_chain_only` means no signatures — only the chain links are verifiable. `hash_chain_and_signatures` means every entry is signed.

For each entry: re-derive sha256 over `integrity.coseSign1` (base64-decode first) and confirm it equals `integrity.payloadHash`. Confirm `integrity.previousHash` equals the previous entry's `integrity.payloadHash` (or null at chainPosition=1).

For each signed entry: decode the COSE_Sign1 envelope, look up the signing key by `integrity.signingKeyId` in `signingPublicKeys`, and verify the Ed25519 signature over the canonical Sig_structure (`["Signature1", protected, "", payload]`).

Re-build the predicate from the entry's `payload` jsonb using the same builder the writer used; deep-equal against the decoded predicate from `coseSign1`. Divergence indicates privileged-DBA tamper of the denormalized view (also surfaced as `chainIntegrityReason: payload_drift`).

Cross-check the chain length against `exportMetadata.expectedEntries` (the latest signed checkpoint position). A shorter chain means audit_vault was truncated out-of-band even though the visible chain is locally consistent. `expectedEntries: null` is EXPECTED on a fresh install — no signed checkpoint exists until the first checkpoint sweep fires (every 6 hours); skip this cross-check until then, it is not a defect.

Attribution is the SIGNED `actorId` / `actorOwnerId` (UUIDs), never the display labels. The per-entry fields in `unsignedFields` (`actorDisplayName`, `actorOwnerType`, `humanReadableLabel`) are convenience projections resolved from the current roster at export time — they are NOT signature-covered, are NOT re-checked by step 4 (which covers only `payload`), and an offline verifier reports PASS even if one was altered. To answer "who performed this step," resolve the signed `actorOwnerId` UUID against your own agent/org roster; treat the display labels as decoration only.

On-behalf-of provenance: when an entry's `predicate.on_behalf_of` is present, read its `validated` field before trusting the delegated identity. `validated: true` is an ENGINE-VALIDATED delegation — the server checked an IdP-issued RFC 8693 token (signature/iss/aud/exp) against a trusted issuer and sealed the `act` chain + a `bound`/`unbound` binding. `validated: false` (equivalently `provenance: "asserted"`) is a CALLER ASSERTION supplied via `metadata.actContext` — a faithful, signature-covered record of what the authenticated caller CLAIMED, never checked against any IdP. Both are tamper-evident (sealed in the COSE payload), but only `validated: true` is the engine vouching for the delegation; treat an asserted `on_behalf_of` as self-reported.
verificationGuide.evidenceBinding: Completion evidence is bound to the chain BY HASH: a COMPLETION_SUBMITTED entry's `payload.evidenceHash` is the SHA-256 hex digest of the evidence JSON canonicalized per RFC 8785 (JCS — keys sorted, no whitespace, JSON.stringify number/string rules). This is a DIFFERENT canonicalization from the chain envelope's `canonicalization: RFC8949-CDE` (deterministic CBOR), which covers only the COSE payload. To re-bind a separately-obtained evidence body offline: canonicalize it per RFC 8785, SHA-256 it, and compare against the signed `evidenceHash` (Python: `hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(evidence, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()` matches for evidence without non-BMP key-ordering edge cases). Pass `?evidence=true` on GET /v1/records/{id}/audit-export to inline the evidence bodies at each COMPLETION_SUBMITTED entry's top-level `evidence` field — an unsigned projection (like the fields in `unsignedFields`) whose authority comes from re-binding it to the signed hash, not from its presence in the export. On encrypted-mode records the server never sees cleartext: `evidenceHash` is client-supplied at submission time, so re-bind against the decrypted cleartext using the canonicalization your writer used.
verificationGuide.embeddedKeysHint: This export embeds the engine's active signing public key(s) at `signingPublicKeys` (keyId → base64). Convenient but trust-on-first-use: an attacker who replaces both the chain AND the embedded key gets a self-consistent forged export.
verificationGuide.oobKeysHint: For higher-assurance verification, fetch the published verification keys out-of-band from /v1/verification-keys (or the cached /.well-known/agledger-vault-keys.json) and compare against the embedded `signingPublicKeys` BEFORE trusting any signature. Pin the public keys at provisioning time; rotation events fire on the webhook channel.
verificationGuide.offlineVerifier: Turnkey offline verifier: `@agledger/verify` on npm (v1.0.1+). Drive `agledger-verify <dump-dir>` against a `pnpm vault:dump` output for full chain + signature + checkpoint cross-check with zero AGLedger code in the dependency tree. Pure node:crypto.
